newsitem.title: USA: US natgas stocks seen up 70-75 bcf in weekly AGAs.
newsitem.headline: US natgas stocks seen up 70-75 bcf in weekly AGAs.

text.p: U.S. natural gas storage levels were expected to rise by 70 to 75 billion cubic feet (bcf) when weekly American Gas Association (AGA) data are released later today, industry sources said Wednesday.
The Reuter poll of industry players showed expectations for an overall build ranged from 57 bcf to 85 bcf for the week ended October 4. The four-week average is 89 bcf.
"The HDDs (heating degree days) were quite a bit higher last week and prices were higher too, so the number may be off a bit (from recent rates)," said one Houston-based trader.

Last week, AGA showed overall storage rose by 84 bcf, slightly above expectations, but was still 275 bcf, or 10 percent, below the same year-ago period. While eastern stocks were at 86 percent of capacity and on target to match 1995 levels, producing region inventories stood at 66 percent full, well-below last year.

Last year at this time, total inventories gained 48 bcf, meaning a build today in the expected range would narrow the gap to last year to about 250 bcf. For the same week in 1995, eastern storage rose by 41 bcf, while producing stocks were up just two bcf.
